data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Pigmentary & cosmeceutical agents_

**Class:** Melanocytotoxic depigmenting agent

## Mechanism of action
- Converted by tyrosinase to reactive quinones → haptens that trigger an immune (melanocyte-specific) response → permanent destruction of melanocytes, even at distant sites

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Permanent depigmentation of remaining normal skin in extensive (universal) vitiligo (>50–80% body surface)
- Never for melasma or cosmetic lightening

## Dose & formulations
- 20% cream once or twice daily to remaining pigmented areas; depigmentation over 4–12 months

## Adverse effects
- Irritant/allergic dermatitis, distant depigmentation (unintended), repigmentation in sun-exposed areas, permanent sun sensitivity
- Psychological impact — counsel carefully (irreversible)

## Contraindications
- Melasma, freckles, PIH (causes irreversible confetti depigmentation), children

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Only for universal vitiligo — permanent
- Different from hydroquinone (which is reversible)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.26 (Monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
